title: Word 1 — On Self-Examination
attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Russian of St Tikhon of Zadonsk (public domain), from the cycle he preached and later published as Краткие нравоучительные слова ("Short Moral-Instructive Words"), St Petersburg, 1784 — 27 sermons ("Слово первое" through "Слово двадцать седьмое") plus a 28th appended piece, "О муке вечной и о жизни вечной" (On Eternal Torment and Eternal Life). Source text: azbyka.ru (https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Tihon_Zadonskij/kratkie-nravouchitelnye-slova/). No prior public-domain English translation of this collection could be found (confirmed via research 2026-08-15); this is, as far as could be verified, the first. The Russian text the translation was made from is kept in the repository.

sections.heading: The glory of the Christian name

pairs.en: Glory to God! All of us are called Christians; all of us confess the one Triune God, the living and immortal God; all of us were baptized in the name of the holy and consubstantial Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; all of us believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of God, crucified and risen from the dead, and in token of this we sign ourselves with the cross; all of us enter the Holy Church and pray, and call upon, sing, and glorify the holy name of God; all of us hear the holy Word of God; all of us partake of the holy and life-giving Mysteries of Christ; all of us are called to eternal life and the heavenly kingdom, and we say in the holy Creed: *“I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come.”* Glory to God for this, and for everything! Truly the Mysteries of Christianity are most glorious and magnificent, hearers! It is great and glorious to be a Christian!

sections.heading: An apostolic summons to test ourselves

pairs.en: But let us look at ourselves and test whether we are true Christians, according to the apostle's exhortation: *“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith”* [2 Corinthians 13:5]. For without faith no one can be a Christian.

We display the marks of Christianity, as was said above — but do we possess true Christianity within? For everything external without the internal is nothing, and outward signs without the truth itself are falsehood and hypocrisy. We all boast of faith, but do we perform works befitting faith, as the apostle says to every one of us: *“Show me thy faith by thy works”* [James 2:18]?

sections.heading: Testing the substance beneath the name

pairs.en: We are called Christians after Christ — but have we crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts, as befits Christians who believe in the crucified Christ, according to the apostle's teaching: *“They that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts”* [Galatians 5:24]? Do we feel within ourselves that joyful spiritual anointing of which the holy Apostle John wrote [1 John 2:27]? We believe the Gospel — but do we live worthily of the Gospel? We confess and call upon the true God — but do we please Him with faith and a pure conscience, as He requires of us? We hear the holy Word of God — but do we heed it and correct ourselves by its rule? We partake of the holy and life-giving Mysteries of the Body and Blood of Christ — but are we renewed by holy Communion, and do we build up within ourselves the spiritual, new man?

Let us examine all this and more: how we live, what manner of people we are, how we think, how we speak, how we act, with what heart we turn to the all-seeing God, and how we deal with one another. And having examined all this, let us correct ourselves, that we may be Christians not only in name but in truth.

By God's grace we have become Christians; let us strive, then, to possess true Christianity within. We were baptized into the one Triune God and received the gift of holiness and justification; let us strive to keep this heavenly treasure to the end. We believe in the crucified Jesus Christ; let us strive to follow Him in faith and, each taking up his own cross, walk after Him. We confess and call upon the heavenly God; let us strive to please Him with heavenly conduct. We hear the Word of God; let us strive to live as it teaches us. We look for the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come; let us strive to live in this world worthily of the resurrection of the dead and eternal life, and, turning away from the vanity of this world, to seek after the eternal blessings alone. We approach the holy and heavenly table of Christ's Mysteries; let us strive that this heavenly, life-giving Bread may bring into us life, sanctification, enlightenment, renewal, joy, and spiritual comfort. So shall we show our faith by our works. So shall we be Christians not only in name but in deed.

*“O God, be merciful unto us, and bless us; and show us the light of Thy countenance, and have mercy upon us; that we may know Thy way upon earth, Thy saving health among all nations”* [Psalm 67:1–2]. Amen.
